title: Vintage Gibson SG Special Value Guide: P-90s And More
description: Read how P-90 and mini-humbucker eras, original finishes and repairs affect vintage SG Special value. Joe explains the comparisons behind an appraisal.
h1: Vintage Gibson SG Special Value Guide
alt: Cherry Gibson SG Special with two black P-90 pickups, a large pickguard and short vibrato

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Gibson SG Special Worth?
faqs.a: An all-original cherry Gibson SG Special from 1961 to 1965, in excellent condition with its original case, falls around $6,000 to $11,000 as of October 2026. I account for the exact year, factory bridge or vibrato and condition before placing a guitar within that broad range.

faqs.q: What Condition Does This Price Range Assume?
faqs.a: All-original examples in excellent condition with original case and no structural repairs. Includes factory wraparound and short-vibrato configurations; case wear varies. I match those details before using the $6,000 to $11,000 range for an individual guitar.

faqs.q: Is A Dealer Offer The Same As The Published Range?
faqs.a: It isn't. The table describes completed-sale comparisons before shipping and tax. A buying offer also accounts for the instrument's condition, selling costs, preparation and the dealer's margin. I explain an offer for the actual guitar rather than promising the top of a general range.

faqs.q: Does A Quality Refret Change The Collector Category?
faqs.a: A quality refret is accepted maintenance and preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise all-original guitar. It takes the instrument out of the museum-quality category. Neck reshaping is a separate alteration.
